clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's death in June 1991, within a few years: your late nights and unsettled feeling from 1989 onward, the move to Hollin Road that autumn, your leaning hard on Rafe once at conservatory in 1991, the wrist injury that stopped your playing that October, the blowup with Rafe in November, your absorption in fixing radios through the winter, your lost and low feeling in early 1992 with him gone and your mother about to remarry, your grandmother Winifred's thyroid surgery around the same time, and your bleak year at community college that followed. Your mother filled in your college forms that spring, and by January 1994 you were stung that your dad had never heard of the film you were making; that same month you found your drive again with the exchange to Lisbon. The shifts pile up across these years with your grandfather's death sitting among them and your grandmother's illness nearby, and no one else's shifts show in these months apart from your mother's move to remarry and your grandmother's health trouble.

clusters.name: Your separation from Joelle, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: Around your bonding with Joelle in early 1998 and your separation in July 1999, within a year and a half: your insomnia began getting in the way in 1999 with sleepless nights before concerts, and at the same time you were playing the best you ever had and winning competitions; the split came in July, and by August you started with a therapist. One shift is you and one is Joelle's, so this belongs to you alone.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's diagnosis with bowel cancer, 2001–2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred's diagnosis with bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, within a couple of years: your running out of steam for performing in September 2001, your disastrous audition for the national orchestra in early 2002, your being on poor terms with family and friends, your leaving Thornbury for Gull Harbour in September 2002, your meeting Marisol in early 2003 and moving to Fenwick that June to live with her, your separation from her by October, and your sinking into deep depression once you split. You returned to Thornbury in late 2003 and could not face your family, though you relied on friends; the depression took hold that winter at its worst. The shifts are yours and no one else's shows across these months.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within months: you went to Alder Creek in July to build with Silas before nursing school, too drained for conversation with your mother, and when she pressed to visit you and drove out regardless in late July, you kept the door shut on her and the visit went wrong. By August you left for nursing school at Marlow Sound and stopped speaking to your mother; the silence held for roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke in early 2009 nearby. Two shifts alone would not hold a period, but your grandmother's death sits among these events and the silence with your mother cuts across them all.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within a couple of years: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along; your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017; your sister Tara was married in summer 2018 and flew for a regional airline; your aunt Imogen's memory was slipping and she lashed out when muddled; your job steadied and paid well by June 2019, but by October that year you were constantly feeling you ought to drive your projects forward and started a sleeping pill. That same October, Wren was swamped with a street party, a fundraising dinner, and the drive to her mother's retirement party at the lake; she was anxious and you were too strict laying out a plan to settle her, and at the lake weekend in late October you were awake from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose, feeling you didn't belong. She talked all day with her father and brother, and once the weekend had a plan the dinner went well and she settled, but you remained distant and anxious on the drive home. Your job steadied and your anxiety eased once you planned shorter, more regular calls with your mother, so the settling edges toward the winter of 2019.
